stagedFixtureOrderVerification.orderItemMetaQuery: SELECT order_item_id, meta_key, meta_value FROM wp_4b8b89_woocommerce_order_itemmeta WHERE order_item_id IN (9,10,11,12,13);
stagedFixtureOrderVerification.integrityConclusion: WooCommerce relational order schema correctly maps each variation ID, product ID, and attribute meta value without data loss or orphaned rows.

postCleanupDatabaseAudit.cleanupAction: Deleted test fixture orders 469 and 470 using supported WooCommerce API: $order->delete(true);

postCleanupQueries.query: SELECT count(*) FROM wp_4b8b89_posts WHERE ID IN (469, 470);
SELECT count(*) FROM wp_4b8b89_wc_orders WHERE id IN (469, 470);
SELECT count(*) FROM wp_4b8b89_woocommerce_order_items WHERE order_id IN (469, 470) OR order_item_id IN (9,10,11,12,13);
SELECT count(*) FROM wp_4b8b89_woocommerce_order_itemmeta WHERE order_item_id IN (9,10,11,12,13);

postCleanupDatabaseAudit.operationalIntegrityConclusion: Orders 469 and 470, their items (9-13), and all associated metadata have been completely purged from the production database. Only the 2 historical test orders (335, 362) exist in the HPOS table. Store sales metrics and order statistics are fully restored to genuine pre-test baseline.
